fact: Connecting Africa reports that SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service launched in Sierra Leone in June 2024.
The communications minister said on 2025-01-31 that three local companies are providing Starlink services in Sierra Leone; the article is dated 2025-01-31 and gives no earlier date for this state.
Semafor reports Sierra Leone granted Starlink a licence about a year before its June 2024 launch, i.e. in 2023 (exact date not given).
Semafor reports Sierra Leone became the 10th African country to launch the Starlink service in June 2024.
A table of Starlink's African markets lists Sierra Leone as 'Available' (no launch date given; as_of is the article's publication date).
Sierra Leone is listed among 26 African countries where Starlink is 'Active Now' (no launch date given; as_of is the article's publication date).
Le360's May 2026 regulatory-status table lists Sierra Leone among countries where Starlink has been granted a licence and is operational; no licence date or licensing body given.
Minister of Communication, Technology and Innovation Salima Bah said in a 30 September 2025 address that Sierra Leone has introduced Starlink satellite internet service.
NatCA Director-General Amara Brewah said Starlink satellite broadband has been licensed in Sierra Leone (no licence date given; as_of is the article date).

NatCA Director-General said Starlink has been operating in Sierra Leone for two years, serving remote clinics, schools and farmers (as_of is the article date; sale to households or businesses is implied, not stated).
